title: The Buried Door
text: You fled the fall of Herevale on coordinates you never chose — numbers mashed into the nav console while the sky burned behind you. The blind jump ends here: an uninhabited world, green-gray and silent. No cities. No signals. No sentient life at all. But the survey pass finds ruins — vast, half-buried geometry that predates every charted civilization — and threading out of them, a trace so faint you almost dismiss it: electromagnetic radiation, patterned, patient, still broadcasting after ten thousand years. You follow it down into the stonework, past a door older than your species, to its source: a data-core resting in a cradle of light. It is damaged — half its lattice burned away — but it is alive.

outcomes.text: The moment you lift it, the EM trace stops — ten thousand years of patient broadcasting, ended because someone finally came. Then the core blooms in your hands: a star-map, vast and broken, pointing one direction — coreward, toward the Pillar. Waypoints flicker across it, smeared with corruption. Regions, not places. You'll have to search every one the hard way. Somewhere far behind you, you imagine the Wake's sensors twitching. Time to move.

options.label: Strip the site for salvage first, then take the core

outcomes.text: The cradle mechanisms alone are worth a fortune in scrap alloy. You work fast, ugly, and profitably — then lift the core. It blooms: a broken star-map pointing coreward, its waypoints smeared into rough regions by corruption. As you climb out of the trench, the horizon flickers with distant drive-flares. You were not the only one who noticed this place.

You get greedy. A support strut gives way and the chamber half-collapses; you drag the core free through the dust, bruised and coughing, leaving the salvage buried. The core still works — it blooms into a broken star-map pointing coreward, waypoints smeared into rough regions. It cost you time you didn't have.

title: The Ruin in the Static
text: This is it — the source the corrupted waypoint could only smear into a region. An Ascended structure, intact, half-swallowed by the terrain, and broadcasting the same lattice-song as your data-core. Inside, the walls answer the core like an old friend finishing a sentence. A new leg of the star-map begins to resolve.

options.label: Decode the next leg and go

outcomes.text: The core drinks from the ruin for an hour and the map sharpens: the next leg of the road coreward, and the jump gate that leads to it. The gate codes are yours. The Wake will find this place eventually — be far away when they do.

options.label: Linger and sweep the site for anything useful

outcomes.text: The map sharpens — the next leg, and the gate codes to reach it. In a collapsed side-gallery you also find a cache: sealed cells of refined drive fuel, still potent after millennia. The Ascended left the lights on for whoever followed.

The map sharpens — the next leg, and the gate codes to reach it. But the deep galleries are stripped bare, and on the way out your loader tears a fuel line that costs you precious reserves. Not every ruin is a gift.

title: A Light in the Long Dark
text: It starts as one pixel on a dead sensor board, and becomes a ship: an ugly, magnificent ore hauler, running lights blazing, matching your drift. The captain doesn't ask who you are — out here, the oldest law of the void is older than any war. They throw you a tow line and haul your cold hull to the nearest port with a working fuel dock.

outcomes.text: The dockmaster counts your scrap twice, then pumps the cells without a word. It isn't much — but the ship is alive again, and alive is everything.
A real refueling, the kind that makes the reactor hum contentedly for the first time in days. You leave the dock poorer and considerably less likely to die in the dark.
Full cells. The dockhands top you off to the safety valves while the hauler crew waves off your thanks and burns back into the black. You won't forget that pixel of light as long as you live.

options.label: You can't afford much — just catch your breath at the dock

outcomes.text: The tow was free; the fuel isn't, and your hold is nearly empty. You drift at the dock, watching ships come and go with tanks full of somewhere else. Something will have to turn up.

title: Teeth in the Dark
text: A dead ship draws scavengers like blood in water. This one comes in slow and confident — a patched-together cutter with a reinforced boarding collar and no transponder, crewed by people who have done this before. They aren't answering hails. They don't need anything you'd give up willingly. They want the ship.

outcomes.text: You meet them at the airlock with everything you have, and it turns out a cornered exile is worth three bored scavengers. They break off trailing atmosphere — and in their scramble they abandon a breach skiff clamped to your hull, fuel cells full. Their loss. Very much your gain.
You fight. It isn't enough. The last thing the ship's log records is cutting torches opening the aft airlock, and then the log stops meaning anything at all.

title: The Long Dark
text: You wait. There is a particular silence a dead ship makes — the reactor banked to embers, the vents whispering on quarter-power, your own heartbeat suddenly the loudest system aboard.

outcomes.text: Nothing. Stars wheel past the viewport with monumental indifference. You reread old logs, ration the water, and try not to do the arithmetic on how far behind you the Wake is.
A contact! — for six agonizing minutes, a drive flare on the boards, growing... and then shrinking. Whoever they were, they had somewhere better to be. The silence afterward is worse than before.

You spend the day at the viewport with the data-core in your lap. Its lattice glimmers faintly toward the Pillar, patient as stone, as if ten thousand years has taught it that someone always comes. You wish you shared its confidence.

title: Contact in the Ashes
text: Wake-held space is not empty space. A picket cutter unfolds from the shadow of a cracked moon, running lights the color of embers, and its targeting array reaches for your hull like a hand. They know what you are. The channel fills with a single repeated word in their liturgical cant: HALT.

outcomes.text: You put your guns into their sensor mast first and their nerve second. The cutter breaks off, venting atmosphere, and you strip a drive cell from the debris it sheds. It cost you plating you'll miss.
It's a mauling, not a duel. You win it — barely — limping clear of the tumbling wreck with your hull groaning and half a cargo rack shot away.
You firewall the throttle and run for the dark, burning reserves like a bonfire. Their pursuit breaks off at the edge of the dead zone — this space is already theirs; they don't need to chase hard.
You escape, but not clean — a parting shot chews through your aft plating as you claw away, and the drive drinks deep the whole way out.

title: Contact in the Ashes
text: Wake-held space is not empty space. A picket cutter unfolds from the shadow of a cracked moon, targeting array reaching for your hull — but your drive is already screaming hot, exactly as you planned. They know what you are. You know how fast you are.

outcomes.text: You put your guns into their sensor mast first and their nerve second. The cutter breaks off, venting atmosphere, and you strip a drive cell from the debris it sheds. It cost you plating you'll miss.
It's a mauling, not a duel. You win it — barely — limping clear of the tumbling wreck with your hull groaning and half a cargo rack shot away.
This is why you came in hot. The cutter's firing solution chases empty space — you're already past it and gone, a rumor in their sensor logs.
One glancing hit scores your dorsal plating as you blow through their picket line — but the drive was hot, the vector was yours, and the dark takes you back cheap.

title: Ancient Ruins
text: Ascended stonework, half-swallowed by the terrain — but your data-core stays silent in its cradle. Whatever sang here went quiet ages ago. This is not the source the map is chasing. It might still be worth the climb down: sites like this fed three generations of relic-hunters, and buried more than a few of them.

outcomes.text: A patient day with cutting tools pays out: intact alloy conduit, sealed mechanisms, trade goods the relic-hunters somehow missed. The stone watches you work and keeps its silence.
The deep galleries were stripped generations ago, but the looters worked sloppy — you pull good salvage out of their own abandoned rigging, and copy a wall of glyphs the codex will want someday.

You are not alone down here. Grave-robbers rise out of the side-galleries with cutting torches and bad intentions — it costs you a scramble back to the ship and a hard burn to break contact, but you keep what you'd already pulled: their stash, and yours.

The doorway was rigged — an old deadfall charge, relic-hunter work, still patient after all these years. The blast brings half the gallery down and you dig yourself out with bleeding hands. Whatever was worth guarding is buried past reaching now.

options.label: Log it and leave it undisturbed

outcomes.text: The core is quiet; the map points elsewhere. You chart the site for the codex and leave its dead songs to the dust.

title: Verdant World
text: A living world, green and loud with weather. No signs of settlement — just forests that have never heard a name and rivers running metal-bright. Setting down costs time, but living worlds are generous.

options.label: Land and process volatiles into fuel

outcomes.text: The refinery rig chews through organics and comes up singing: usable drive fuel, cleaner than anything you could buy.
A storm front rolls in mid-process and you have to lift early, cells half-full and one intake fouled.
The biosphere fights back — spores foul every intake within the hour. You strip and purge the rig and lift with nothing to show for the landing.

options.label: Stay in orbit — just survey and move on

outcomes.text: You chart it, name it in your own head, and leave it in peace. If anyone from Herevale is still alive out there, maybe someday this is where they land.

title: The Empty Streets
text: A colony world, abandoned in a hurry — years ago by the dust, not centuries. Meals still on tables. A whole town holding its breath. Whatever they fled, it came from the sky.

outcomes.text: You fill the hold with alloy stock, sealed rations, and a working compressor. You try not to look at the family photos still stuck to the walls.
Automated defenses — still loyal to owners years gone — drive you off with your shields scorched. You get away with a sack of fittings and your heart pounding.
Some places want to be left alone. You mark the site on your charts and burn for open sky.

title: The Screaming Meridian
text: A gas-wreathed rock whose upper atmosphere is one permanent storm. Your sensors flag dense pockets of charged volatiles riding the wind — free fuel, if you're willing to fly into that.

outcomes.text: White knuckles, one cracked viewport, and intake cells brimming. The ship smells like ozone for days. Worth it.
The storm nearly eats you. You claw back to orbit with torn plating and barely more fuel than the attempt cost.
The volatile pocket collapses the moment your intakes bite — the whole run is turbulence and static for nothing. You abort with scorched plating and empty cells.
You watch the storm chew its own horizon for a while, log the readings, and move on.

title: Waystation
text: A rattletrap trade station clinging to the local star's L4 point, run by a family who ask no questions and watch your hands the whole time. The fuel price is honest. Nothing else about the place is.

options.label: Trade scrap for fuel (2 scrap → 3 fuel)

outcomes.text: The exchange is quick and wordless. As you undock, the station's sensor dish tracks you a moment too long. You hope they sell fuel to everyone — and information to no one.

options.label: Just dock, stretch your legs, listen to the chatter

outcomes.text: Dock gossip: shipping lanes gone quiet trailing-side, whole systems dark. They talk about the Wake the way coastal towns talk about weather. Nobody says the word 'exile,' but a few eyes linger on you.
A deckhand quietly slips you a cell of fuel and won't take payment. 'Had cousins on one of the burned worlds,' she says. 'Go. Don't stop.'

title: The Toll Ring
text: The station's docking ring is controlled by a local junta squadron running an 'inspection tariff' racket. Their cutters are faster than you. The polite fiction is that this is voluntary.

outcomes.text: You pay. They wave you through with the bored contempt of men who will never have to run from anything. The hold is lighter; the ship is intact.
You thread the cutter patrol on cold thrusters and burn out of their envelope before they commit to a chase. Free — but you spent fuel like water doing it.
A warning shot clips your aft plating before you clear the ring. You get away — poorer in hull patching than the tariff would have cost.

title: Cold Hulk
text: A freighter, decades dead, tumbling end over end. Holed by weapons fire — old-pattern, not Wake. Its transponder still whispers a name nobody will ever answer to again.

options.label: Suit up and cut your way in

outcomes.text: The cargo bay is a treasury of alloy and sealed parts. The crew compartments you don't linger in. You take what keeps you flying and leave the rest to the dark.
The hulk's spin is worse than it looked; a shifting bulkhead nearly pins you, and you abandon the sweep with a half-empty sack and a torn glove seal.
Its reactor is somehow still warm — and unstable. You grab what's in reach and push off hard before the whole hulk vents in a slow blue flare.

options.label: Scan and pass — you don't like the look of it

outcomes.text: The scan logs the wreck's story for your charts: hit while running, engines first. Somebody wanted them stopped, not dead. You leave the ghost to its orbit.

title: The Looping Signal
text: An automated distress beacon, still broadcasting from a lifeboat cluster fused to a shattered hull. The loop is old. The odds of survivors are almost nothing. Almost.

outcomes.text: No one. Frost on the inside of every faceplate. You cut the beacon so it stops calling to nobody, and take the lifeboats' untouched supply cells as inheritance.
The 'beacon' is bait — a scavenger snare rigged to mag-clamp your airlock. You tear free with dented plating and your dignity somewhere back in the debris field.
You can't check every ghost in this arm. You log the position and tell yourself someone with more fuel and fewer hunters will come. You almost believe it.

title: The Bright Shoal
text: A drifting shoal of ionized gas, dense and charged — the kind of pocket drive engineers write love letters about. Your intakes could drink straight from it.

outcomes.text: The shoal pours into your cells like it was waiting for you. Best refueling this side of a depot, and nobody to pay.
Midway through the harvest the shoal destabilizes and discharges across your hull — you break off with a partial load and tripped breakers all over the ship.
The shoal thins and scatters before your intakes finish deploying — solar wind got there first. You drift through glitter too sparse to drink.

options.label: Too exposed out here. Skip it.

outcomes.text: Free fuel draws every tank-dry drifter and pirate in the sector, and you're in no shape to meet them. You slide past the glow and keep your silhouette dark.

title: Sensor Ghost
text: For six full seconds, your sensors swear there is a ship alongside you — matching velocity, twenty meters off your port hull, silent on every band. Then nothing. The log shows six seconds of a contact that cannot exist.

outcomes.text: You burn hard down the ghost's last vector and find... a knot of reflective dust, dead sensors' honest mistake. Probably. You top off nothing, learn nothing, and can't stop checking your port viewport for the rest of the day.
The vector dead-ends in a pocket of debris — centuries old, unfamiliar alloy, faintly warm. You bring a few kilos aboard. Your data-core hums a fraction louder with it in the hold.
Every long-haul crew has a ghost story. Now you have yours. You write it down, and you do not chase it.

title: The Rip
text: A gravitational shear line scars this volume — some ancient violence bent space here and it never fully healed. Ships can sling off it for a free boost. Ships have also come apart trying.

options.label: Ride the shear for a slingshot

outcomes.text: The ship groans down to her keel bolts — and the shear hurls you out the far side with your jump cells brim-charged. A month of fuel economy in one terrifying minute.
You misjudge the gradient. The shear rattles the ship like a die in a cup, sheds gear through a sprung cargo seal, and spits you out barely ahead on charge.
The shear shrugs you off its shoulder — no slingshot, no boost, just a long queasy tumble back to flat space and a ship full of rattled crockery.
Whatever tore space here might still be listening for ripples. You go around, the long way, like a sensible person fleeing a genocidal armada.

title: Eyes in the Dark
text: Your threat board pings once and goes quiet: a Wake reconnaissance probe, dormant until your drive signature woke it. It is already turning its antenna trailing-ward — toward the fleet front. Toward them.

outcomes.text: One clean shot and the probe becomes expanding glitter — antenna still folded, nothing sent. The dark stays quiet behind you.
The kill is clean, but a probe going dark is its own kind of message. Somewhere along the front, a watch officer marks the silence on a chart — and the hunt leans your way.

It transmits as it dies — a long, deliberate pulse aimed trailing-ward, and your shot arrives half a breath too late. Somewhere behind you, ash-colored hulls change heading. The hunt just got a fresher scent.

options.label: Run silent and sneak past it

outcomes.text: You cut thrust, drift dark between rocks, and let the probe's gaze sweep past. An hour of held breath, and then you're gone — unlogged, unnamed, unhunted. For now.
Halfway through the drift its antenna twitches and tracks you — one short burst, trailing-ward, before you clear its cone. Not a full fix, but enough. The hunt tightens.
